keyframe_review.note: 137,946 km2 for 353-591, a block of Tamil Nadu from the Kaveri delta to Madurai (8.1-12.9 N, 76.0-80.2 E). The page has no infobox area and no map (it cites Schwartzberg's atlas only), so the area check is not possible; the page says only 'rulers of all or parts of Tamil region' and 'sometime between the 3rd century and 6th century CE', so the shape stands as an unverified soft block. The 'Established: 3rd century CE' infobox is earlier than Cliopatria's 353; no page dates the start. Reviewer (sa-02-e, 2026-10-19): the shape holds 353-574 only; from 575 the northern Tamil country is Pallava (the 575 loss in the ledger), see the next keyframe.

keyframe_review.note: 61,508 km2 for 592-601, the northern part (10.0-12.9 N) after the south goes to the Pandya shape. The Kalabhra page says Simhavishnu 'consolidated his kingdom from south of the Krishna river and up to the Kaveri river by c. 575 CE' (the Late Pallava dossier records the matching 575 gain), so the part of the rump north of about 11.8 N is Pallava, not Kalabhra; the page also says the dynasty 'ended for certain by the last quarter of 6th century', so the 592-601 rump itself rests on Cliopatria alone. Kept in reduced form, unverified.

ledger.note: 353: the Kalabhras hold the Tamil country. The page dates the dynasty only to 'sometime between the 3rd century and 6th century CE' (infobox 'Established: 3rd century CE'); the year 353 and the extent are Cliopatria's, the page is silent. They 'defeated the Cholas, Pandyas, and Cheras and established their rule'.

ledger.note: c. 575: the Pallavas take the northern Tamil country. 'Simhavishnu consolidated his kingdom from south of the Krishna river and up to the Kaveri river by c. 575 CE.' The matching gain is in the Late Pallava dossier; Cliopatria draws it in 602 and keeps the Kalabhra shape whole until 591.

ledger.note: c. 590: the Pandya kingdom is revived at Madurai. 'The Pandya kingdom was revived by king Kadungon c. 560-590 CE'; Karashima 'dated Kadunkon's reign to 560 - 590 CE'. The page gives no separate date for the expulsion, so the year 592 is Cliopatria's.

ledger.note: 601: the Kalabhra rule is over. 'The Kalabhras dynasty had ended for certain by the last quarter of 6th century'; 'was defeated and ended by the Chalukyas, Pandyas, and Pallavas'. The page gives no year; 601 is Cliopatria's last year, one year past the page's 'last quarter of the 6th century'. The remnant passes to the Pandyas (Kadungon, 'destroyer' of the Kalabhras in the Velvikudi plates) in this reading; the Pallava share is the 575 loss above.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages, both used. The Kalabhra article gives no founding year, no area and no map; everything about extent (353 start, 601 end, the 592 split) is Cliopatria's and is recorded at confidence 1. Reconciled with the Late Pallava dossier (sa-02 part with the Pallavas), which dates Simhavishnu's gain of the Tamil country up to the Kaveri to c. 575 from this page: the Kalabhra dossier records the matching loss at 575 and reduces the 592-601 rump; Cliopatria itself draws the Pallava gain only in 602 and keeps a Kalabhra rump to 601 that no page supports, so a gap-filler should open 'Simhavishnu' and 'Pallava dynasty'. The three Sangam predecessors end in 305 in Cliopatria, 48 years before this row begins; the Kalabhra page says they 'defeated the Cholas, Pandyas, and Cheras' without a date. The Pulankurichi inscription of 'Chendan Kurran (Kootran) dated to 270 CE' is the earliest Kalabhra-linked epigraph on the page but is not taken as a founding date. Rulers: only Achyuta Vikranta is named (5th century, Buddhadatta), with no reign years, so no ruler strip.
